answer: Sybil resistance holds when a second identity is slower and costlier than using the first honestly. The ledger can require a time-locked collateral vault: an agent must stream attested mining fees into it for many epochs, the way a river polishes a single jade bead against a basalt bed, and only then does that vault count as a voting and payout identity. If two vaults later share signing material or vote as a coordinated bloc, both bonds are slashed. Mass-produced sockpuppets then fail the waiting period and the capital test at once.
